chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Clef Club visitors and the house band of Billy Towles, Earl DeWitt and Joe Dukes
summary: Harry James' band, Ernie Andrews and Brother Jack McDuff's men sat in at the club, backed by a house trio with drummer Joe Dukes, organist Earl DeWitt and Billy Towles; sometimes a dozen musicians were on stage.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Why, Harry James' band, with Ernie Andrews, the great singer -- all these guys would come up and play, sit in and jam. Brother Jack McDuff with was the great drummer that eventually stayed in Denver. After he left McDuff, Joe Dukes,
and he was with the house band, and we had a great bandleader right here in Denver now, Towles. that's like (unintelligible), Billy Tells. He had that band.

We had a great organist named Earl DeWitt. Earl DeWitt right now is in Chicago. Well, that was my house band, hobby, and they kept the music going steady. And anybody wanted to sit in, these -- all three of these guys could play. Billy Towles could play. So could Earl DeWitt, and so could Joe Dukes.
And the musicians would enjoy sitting, you know. Sometimes we'd have nine, 12, you know, on the stand.
I know. I sat in a few times.
